messages:
Priya: Heads up — BrightPath demo just hit a bunch of 429s during their data import step. They were doing a 10k-record import, concurrent up to 8 threads.
Alex: Can you paste the error snippet and tenant id? 429 message text helps (per-route vs global).
Priya: tenant=brightpath-prod, route=/v1/generate/chat, timestamp~2509876500. Log: ```ERROR: request rejected status=429 reason=per_route_token_budget_exceeded tokens=12456 route=/v1/generate/chat tenant=brightpath-prod```
Michael: That looks like per-route token budget kicking in (not global). Are they using long-context streaming? 12456 tokens in a short window is consistent with burst.
Emily: Customer wants us to keep the demo running — can we temporarily lift caps for them? they'll pay for overage if needed. Need ETA on fix.
Alex: Short-term options: 1) apply a temporary per-route softcap bump for the tenant (admin action) 2) enable a short grace window that increases burst allowance for 5m 3) advise client to add client-side backoff and reduce concurrency. Which do we prefer?
Priya: Prefer an admin bump for the demo window (15m), plus the grace window if it's quick. Client can't change their importer right now.
Michael: I can enable a temporary bump but need to validate isolation — asking infra if capacity available. Also want the exact request pattern (qps + avg tokens per req).
Priya: Sample pattern: 8 threads x ~3 concurrent requests each ~500 tokens avg = ~12k tokens/sec peak for ~2m windows.
Alex: OK. To be safe I'll do a soft increase to per-route token_budget from 10k -> 25k for tenant brightpath-prod for 20 minutes. That should stop 429s. Will post after done.
ops-bot: scheduled action: grant-per-route-bump tenant=brightpath-prod old=10000 new=25000 duration=20m requested_by=Alex job_id=jb_20250319_01
Alex: Done — I applied the bump. Please confirm if 429s stop.
Priya: Confirmed with customer — errors dropped within a minute. Thanks.
Michael: I'll follow up post-mortem to determine whether per-route budgeting or traffic shape needs permanent tuning. If they consistently do large imports we should discuss a reserved capacity / Dedicated plan with them.
Emily: I'll capture pricing options and proposal for reserved capacity + overage terms; looping legal for SOW.
Priya: Filing a short incident note in follow-up. For now demo is green. Thanks team :raised_hands:
